outcome.technical:
DESIGN, option (b), at the replay. A `ts` is one second, and two writers' same-second rows carry no order: neither file records the other, and read_all's tie-break by file name is an order to print in. Option (a), sub-second stamps, only narrows the window (two processes, clock granularity, rows from other hosts merged later), and every existing row keeps one-second precision. The row format, chain and COMPATIBILITY.md are therefore untouched. The merge driver's `_tie_faults` already works from the same premise.

CHANGES (all four in the declared files):
- `_journal_io.last_words(rows, words_of)` -> `{key: set(words)}`. For each key: every writer's last word in the newest second that speaks of it; one writer's rows stay in append order (keyed by `_file`); a row older than the held second is passed over. read_all's docstring now says its cross-file tie order is not causal and points here.
- drive-phase `confirmed_in_advance` covers a task only when `last_words == {risk.confirmed}`. A reopen sharing the newest second from another writer cancels: the gate asks again. The id parse moved, unchanged, into `_confirmed_ids`.
- drive-phase `standing_review_fix` carries a hand-back only when every possible newest re-open is the drive's hand-back. Otherwise `spent` says the newest re-opens were written by two writers in one second.
- tests/test_drive_phase.py: hr3 made deterministic. It plants the session-less writer token as `ffffffffffffffff` (sorting after drive-fixture-session) and pins both verbs' clock to one second via the suite's own `_pinned_clock`. It asserts its own precondition (same ts, two files, the reopen's file first) as well as the high-risk stop. New: hr4-hr9 (confirm/reopen ties: both file orders, a later second, another task, same-file order both ways) and hr10-hr12 (hand-back ties). hr6/hr7/hr8/hr11/hr12 are the over-fire twins.
- tests/test__journal_io.py: lw1a/lw1b, lw2-lw7, lw8a/lw8b (lw8 goes through append + read_all on disk).

outcome.descriptive: When two journal files hold rows from the same second, they no longer replay in file-name order: a reopen in the same second as a high-risk confirmation now makes the drive ask again. hr3 is deterministic.

hr10-hr12: a drive hand-back is not carried when a human's re-open shares its second from another writer; it is carried when appended later in one file, or a second later
